decisions.reason: The devore line has several variants and is cheap to keep in an existing stocked collection, but trend-driven decorative fabrics are often rotated out after about three seasons, so the option stays open with moderate drop risk.

This transparent burnout line fits the core decoration range and costs little to keep while reorder demand from retailers persists, though its fashion-driven nature means it could be replaced in the next collection change.
As a single burnout article overlapping with the other burnout and devore lines, it is the most likely to be cut in a range cleanup, but there is no evidence of failure and holding costs are low.
Velour-like upholstery fabric is a durable segment with steadier demand than trend-led decoration fabrics, so keeping it preserves upside at modest cost.
A flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric is a staple for contract and retail buyers who depend on reorder continuity, so its value is fairly certain and it should be kept.
A polyester satin lining is a basic complementary article supporting made-to-measure sewing and the wider range, with low uncertainty and low holding cost.
